packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-05 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure: nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading for this packet. This is a blind reading.
Beyond the rules: to look more closely I made enlarged copies (macOS sips, longest side 1400 px) of image-002, -003 and -004 in a scratch folder (b17/zoom05/). No other files were opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 (overview) shows the spine of a bound volume with the boards gone, photographed next to a colour chart and ruler. The photo is rotated about 180 degrees: the chart lettering and the paper shelf label ("16") are upside down. The manuscript text on the spine lining reads the right way up in the image as delivered, so the lining is mounted upside down relative to the book.
- The lining is a parchment or paper strip glued across the spine, cut by three raised sewing bands, so it shows as three separate panels. Top panel (between the label area and the upper band): image-004. Middle panel (between the two bands): image-003. Bottom panel (just below the lower band, two lines only): image-002. image-005 is the label area at the head: only faint ghost/offset traces show there, nothing legible.
- What shows is one column of a gothic textualis/semi-textualis book hand, heavily abbreviated. Each panel shows only a narrow strip, about 15-25 characters per line. Both line ends are lost: on the left to the spine cracking and adhesive, on the right where the strip turns onto the leaf edges. No rubric, initial, running title or gloss is visible. One red/orange spot in image-004 line 8 looks like a stain or a rubrication remnant; I cannot tell which.
- Vertical cracks from the spine folds cross every line and destroy letters at regular intervals.
- Order of panels top to bottom of the image: 004, 003, 002. I cannot tell whether that is the order of the text, because the strip may also be inverted relative to the original page.

image-002 (bottom panel, 2 lines; anything below is lost or blank)

002.02  ti?esse?/ti?e?le  .  ut  tho.  ?n (cut)
   - "tho." has a visible abbreviation point or stroke. I read the letters only and do not expand them.

LEGIBLE WORDS WITH REASONABLE CONFIDENCE
repellit; a p(ar)te; possit; solo; aut; veniat; immedia-; ut tho.; in; multo(?); ꝯtinet(?) or ꝯtenet(?). Taken together, the vocabulary looks like scholastic prose (e.g. "intrinsec-", "praeter", "immediate", "possit"). That is an interpretation, not an observation.

SELECTED / UNREAD
I read every line visible on all three panels. Nothing legible remains unread on these images. Most of each line is physically lost or hidden off-strip, not merely hard to read.

LIMITATIONS AND SUGGESTIONS
- Each line keeps only 3-5 words, with both ends lost. The vertical spine cracks break letters, so many readings are letter-shape guesses.
- The photo is a phone overview with tiles scaled up from it; the resolution limits the reading. A raking-light or higher-resolution straight-on shot of each panel would help, and so would an image of the other side of the lining or of any stubs showing at the gutters, which could show full lines.
- image-005: only ghost/offset traces; no text could be read.
